title: Video and audio surveillance / recording maintenance - 2025 handbook
summary: 2025 handbook policy governing audio/video equipment on RTEC vehicles and property, notice, ownership, viewing/access, law-enforcement/legal disclosure, accident-recording retention and equipment maintenance.

claims.claim: RTEC states that audio/video equipment may be placed on vehicles and property for passenger/public safety, driver management and general security, and that notices are to be posted where equipment is located.

evidence.page_or_section: printed page 43 - Video Surveillance & Audio Policy

claims.claim: The posted-notice language states that people entering/riding in recorded vehicles/property acknowledge their image and/or voice may be recorded and that they have no reasonable expectation of privacy in the recording.

Ownership of vehicle/property audio-video recordings rests exclusively with RTEC; recordings may be provided for accident/criminal investigations or defense and may be produced pursuant to court order, subpoena or other legal process.

RTEC may view cameras/listen to audio for reasons including employee performance review, accident investigation, passenger/driver complaints, equipment maintenance/testing, criminal investigation or other reasons determined by RTEC.

evidence.page_or_section: printed page 44 - Viewing and Monitoring Policy

claims.claim: The Executive Director designates authorized recording reviewers; the handbook names the Safety & Security Officer, Operations Manager, Human Resource Manager and IT technician among those with access, plus others designated by the Executive Director.

evidence.page_or_section: printed page 44 - Viewing and Monitoring Policy

claims.claim: Law-enforcement review is subject to the Executive Director's decision unless lawful court process/subpoena requires production.

evidence.page_or_section: printed page 44 - Viewing and Monitoring Policy

claims.claim: Recordings retained for accident investigation are to be kept for three years after the event or until litigation reaches final resolution; other retained recordings follow the record-retention policy.

evidence.note: The handbook also notes different camera systems retain for different periods and RTEC does not guarantee retention when it has no notice of an investigation.

claims.claim: RTEC is to check vehicle recording equipment at least once every three months, operators/maintenance personnel are to report malfunctioning equipment to the Operations Manager, and daily pre-trip/post-trip checks are described as a practice.

trigger: Operation, review, disclosure, retention or maintenance of RTEC audio/video recording equipment.
prerequisites: Authorized RTEC role or Executive Director designation for review/access where applicable.
steps: Retain accident-related recordings for the stated period and other recordings under the retention policy.
Route external/legal access through the Executive Director or lawful process.
decisions: Whether a recording is retained for accident/other investigation
Whether law enforcement may review absent compulsory legal process
Who is designated to review recordings
deadlines: Accident-investigation recordings: three years after the event or until litigation is finally resolved.
Vehicle recording equipment: operation check once every three months; daily pre/post-trip checks are described as practice.
exceptions: Actual system retention varies by equipment, and the handbook states RTEC does not guarantee a specific retention period when not on notice of an accident or other investigation.
unresolved_questions: Locate and ingest the separate record-retention policy referenced by this section.
Confirm current named roles and access-control implementation for recording systems.
automation_candidates: Retention hold workflow when an accident/complaint/litigation notice is opened.
Quarterly camera inspection and malfunction-remediation tracking.
Access/audit log for recording review and external disclosure.
